subproblem.title: An integrable density is a difference of two finite measures
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (σ-finiteness is not assumed), and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-integrable. Then there are finite measures ν⁺ and ν⁻ on ℝ^P such that ∫ b dν⁺ − ∫ b dν⁻ = ∫ b g dμ for every Borel measurable function b : ℝ^P → ℝ that is bounded, i.e. |b(x)| ≤ C for some constant C and all x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g μ → ∃ νpos νneg : Measure (Eucl P), IsFiniteMeasure νpos ∧ IsFiniteMeasure νneg ∧ ∀ b : Eucl P → ℝ, Measurable b → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, |b x| ≤ C) → ∫ x, b x ∂νpos - ∫ x, b x ∂νneg = ∫ x, b x * g x ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the supplied proof of polyhedral_approx_measure_uniqueness: the measures ν_i^± and the identity behind (★), for one integrable density. The supplied proof applies this to μ_i⌞L, on which g_i is integrable. Here the a.e.-measurable density ofReal ∘ (±g) is used directly, instead of first choosing a Borel version h of g. Every lemma named below is in scope under the frozen GMT.Ch06.Submission imports.

Throughout, r⁺ := max(r, 0) for r ∈ ℝ, and ofReal r ∈ [0, ∞) ⊆ [0, ∞] denotes r⁺ viewed as an extended nonnegative real (ENNReal.ofReal).

1. (Definition.) Put νpos := μ.withDensity (x ↦ ofReal(g(x))) and νneg := μ.withDensity (x ↦ ofReal(−g(x))).

2. (Finiteness.) νpos(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ ≤ ∫⁻ |g| dμ < ∞, since a μ-integrable g has finite integral. Likewise νneg(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻ ofReal(−g) dμ ≤ ∫⁻ |−g| dμ < ∞. So both measures are finite. (Lean: isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal applied to hg.2 : HasFiniteIntegral g μ, and to hg.neg.2.)

3. (Integrals against νpos and νneg.) g is μ-integrable, hence μ-a.e. measurable. So x ↦ ofReal(g(x)) and x ↦ ofReal(−g(x)) are μ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal, applied to g and to x ↦ −g(x)), and they are finite everywhere (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). For such densities, integration against the withDensity measure is integration of the real density times the integrand (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀). Since (ofReal r).toReal = r⁺ (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal'), for every b : ℝ^P → ℝ:
   ∫ b dνpos = ∫ g(x)⁺ b(x) dμ(x),  ∫ b dνneg = ∫ (−g(x))⁺ b(x) dμ(x).

4. (Integrability.) Fix a Borel measurable b with |b(x)| ≤ C for all x.
   - g⁺ = max(g, 0) and (−g)⁺ = max(−g, 0) are μ-integrable (Integrable.pos_part applied to g and to −g).
   - b is measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, and ‖b(x)‖ ≤ C for all x.
   - So g⁺·b and (−g)⁺·b are μ-integrable: a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable factor times an integrable function is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul, then commute the product).

5. (Combination.) By step 3, linearity of the integral for the two integrable functions of step 4 (integral_sub), and the identity r⁺ − (−r)⁺ = r (max_zero_sub_max_neg_zero_eq_self):
   ∫ b dνpos − ∫ b dνneg = ∫ (g(x)⁺ − (−g(x))⁺) b(x) dμ = ∫ g(x) b(x) dμ = ∫ b(x) g(x) dμ.
   This holds for every bounded Borel b, which proves the claim with ν⁺ := νpos and ν⁻ := νneg. ∎
proof_key_steps: Define νpos := μ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ g) and νneg := μ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ (−g)).
Both are finite because ∫⁻ ofReal(±g) dμ ≤ ∫⁻ |g| dμ < ∞ (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal).
∫ b dνpos = ∫ g⁺ b dμ and ∫ b dνneg = ∫ (−g)⁺ b dμ for every b (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal').
For bounded Borel b, g⁺b and (−g)⁺b are μ-integrable (Integrable.pos_part, Integrable.bdd_mul).

audit.reason: The type exactly includes integrability of g and measurability and boundedness of b, without imposing σ-finiteness. The a.e.-measurable positive and negative densities define finite measures. Bounded multiplication supplies the integrability needed for subtraction, and the positive-part identity proves the conclusion. The supplied proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Finite measures agreeing on smooth test functions in an open set agree on functions vanishing outside it
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ν₁ and ν₂ be finite measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P, and let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Suppose ∫ ψ dν₁ = ∫ ψ dν₂ for every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ (smooth of every finite order) with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O. Then ∫ b dν₁ = ∫ b dν₂ for every function b : ℝ^P → ℝ with b(x) = 0 for all x ∉ O. Integrals are Bochner integrals, so a non-integrable function has integral 0; no measurability or boundedness of b is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν₁ ν₂ : Measure (Eucl P)), IsFiniteMeasure ν₁ → IsFiniteMeasure ν₂ → ∀ O : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen O → (∀ ψ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ O → ∫ x, ψ x ∂ν₁ = ∫ x, ψ x ∂ν₂) → ∀ b : Eucl P → ℝ, (∀ x, x ∉ O → b x = 0) → ∫ x, b x ∂ν₁ = ∫ x, b x ∂ν₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the supplied proof of polyhedral_approx_measure_uniqueness (Radon–Nikodym with respect to λ₁ + λ₂, then IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero on O), isolated here for two arbitrary finite measures. The supplied proof gets the density identity from integral_rnDeriv_smul. That lemma, Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq and Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv live in Mathlib files (RadonNikodym, IntegralRNDeriv) that the frozen GMT.Ch06.Submission header does not import. Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.Lebesgue is imported, so step 2 derives the identity from the Lebesgue decomposition. Every lemma named below is in scope under the frozen imports.

Throughout, ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra.

1. (Common reference measure.) Put ν := ν₁ + ν₂, a finite measure. For i = 1, 2 we have ν_i ≤ ν, hence ν_i ≪ ν: if ν(s) = 0 then ν_i(s) ≤ ν(s) = 0. (Lean: Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.rfl.add_right ν₂ gives ν₁ ≪ ν₁ + ν₂. For ν₂, rewrite ν₁ + ν₂ = ν₂ + ν₁ with add_comm and use Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.rfl.add_right ν₁.)

2. (Each ν_i has a density with respect to ν.) Fix i ∈ {1, 2} and let ρ_i := ν_i.rnDeriv ν : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], a measurable function (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv).
   - ν_i and ν are finite, so the pair has a Lebesgue decomposition (the HaveLebesgueDecomposition instance is found automatically): ν_i = ν_i.singularPart ν + ν.withDensity ρ_i (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add ν_i ν).
   - The singular part is mutually singular with ν, is ≤ ν_i, and ν_i ≪ ν. A measure that is both absolutely continuous and singular with respect to ν is zero, so ν_i.singularPart ν = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac applied to ν_i ≪ ν).
   - Hence ν_i = ν.withDensity ρ_i.

3. (Integration against ν_i.) Since ν_i is finite, ρ_i < ∞ ν-almost everywhere (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top ν_i ν). Put f_i(x) := (ρ_i(x)).toReal ∈ [0, ∞). For a measurable, ν-a.e. finite density, integrating any function c against ν.withDensity ρ_i equals integrating x ↦ f_i(x)·c(x) against ν (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul with Measure.measurable_rnDeriv and Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top). This identity holds for every c : ℝ^P → ℝ: both sides use the Bochner convention, and c is integrable for ν.withDensity ρ_i exactly when f_i·c is integrable for ν. With step 2 we get, for every c : ℝ^P → ℝ,
   (∗) ∫ c dν_i = ∫ f_i(x) c(x) dν(x).

4. (The densities are ν-integrable.) ρ_i is measurable and ∫⁻ ρ_i dν ≤ ν_i(ℝ^P) < ∞ (Measure.lintegral_rnDeriv_lt_top, using that ν_i is finite). So f_i = (ρ_i)·toReal is ν-integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top). Hence F := f₁ − f₂ is ν-integrable, so F is locally integrable on O with respect to ν (Integrable.locallyIntegrable, then LocallyIntegrable.locallyIntegrableOn O).

5. (F annihilates smooth tests supported in O.) Let ψ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O.
   - ψ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous) with compact support, and f_i is ν-integrable, hence locally integrable. So x ↦ ψ(x) f_i(x) is ν-integrable (LocallyIntegrable.integrable_smul_left_of_hasCompactSupport).
   - By linearity of the integral (integral_sub) and (∗) with c = ψ (commuting the product ψ(x) f_i(x) = f_i(x) ψ(x)):
     ∫ ψ F dν = ∫ ψ f₁ dν − ∫ ψ f₂ dν = ∫ ψ dν₁ − ∫ ψ dν₂ = 0.
   The last equality is the hypothesis applied to ψ.

6. (F vanishes a.e. on O.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, O is open, and ν is a measure on ℝ^P.
   - By step 4, F is locally integrable on O. By step 5, ∫ ψ(x)·F(x) dν(x) = 0 for every ψ with ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ, compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O. The smoothness class ∞ in that Mathlib lemma is exactly ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) used here, so the hypothesis applies verbatim.
   - IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero therefore gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ O implies F(x) = 0, i.e. f₁(x) = f₂(x).

7. (Conclusion.) Let b : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy b(x) = 0 for all x ∉ O.
   - For ν-a.e. x we have f₁(x) b(x) = f₂(x) b(x). If x ∈ O this follows from step 6. If x ∉ O, then b(x) = 0 and both sides are 0.
   - Functions that agree ν-a.e. have equal Bochner integrals, with no measurability needed (integral_congr_ae). So by (∗) with c = b,
     ∫ b dν₁ = ∫ f₁ b dν = ∫ f₂ b dν = ∫ b dν₂. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := ν₁ + ν₂ is finite and ν₁ ≪ ν, ν₂ ≪ ν.
Lebesgue decomposition plus absolute continuity (haveLebesgueDecomposition_add, singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac): ν_i = ν.withDensity(ν_i.rnDeriv ν).
(∗) ∫ c dν_i = ∫ f_i·c dν for every c, where f_i = (ν_i.rnDeriv ν)·toReal is ν-integrable (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul, lintegral_rnDeriv_lt_top).
∫ ψ·(f₁ − f₂) dν = 0 for every C^∞ ψ with compact support in O, by (∗) and the hypothesis.
For b vanishing outside O, f₁b = f₂b ν-a.e.; conclude ∫ b dν₁ = ∫ b dν₂ by (∗).

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean type agree, including the unrestricted function b. Each proof step is justified: finite-measure Lebesgue decomposition supplies integrable densities, smooth-test uniqueness identifies them on O, and vanishing outside O gives equality of the weighted integrands almost everywhere. The density integration identity genuinely applies without measurability or integrability of b. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Integrable densities agreeing on smooth tests in an open set agree on bounded Borel functions supported there
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ₁ and μ₂ be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (σ-finiteness is not assumed), let g₁ : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ₁-integrable and g₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ₂-integrable, and let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Suppose ∫ ψ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ ψ g₂ dμ₂ for every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O. Then ∫ b g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ b g₂ dμ₂ for every Borel measurable bounded function b : ℝ^P → ℝ (|b(x)| ≤ C for some constant C) with b(x) = 0 for all x ∉ O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g₁ g₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g₁ μ₁ → Integrable g₂ μ₂ → ∀ O : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen O → (∀ ψ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ O → ∫ x, ψ x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, ψ x * g₂ x ∂μ₂) → ∀ b : Eucl P → ℝ, Measurable b → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, |b x| ≤ C) → (∀ x, x ∉ O → b x = 0) → ∫ x, b x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, b x * g₂ x ∂μ₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–6 of the supplied proof of polyhedral_approx_measure_uniqueness. The measures μ_i⌞L there are replaced by arbitrary measures μ_i on which g_i is integrable. The construction of ν_i^± (supplied steps 2–3) is the sibling polyhedral_approx_density_split. The Radon–Nikodym / distribution step (supplied step 5) is the sibling polyhedral_approx_finite_smooth_ext. Every other lemma named below is in scope under the frozen GMT.Ch06.Submission imports.

1. (Split both signed measures.) Apply polyhedral_approx_density_split to (μ₁, g₁) and to (μ₂, g₂). This gives finite measures p₁, n₁, p₂, n₂ on ℝ^P such that, for i = 1, 2 and every Borel measurable bounded c : ℝ^P → ℝ,
   ∫ c dp_i − ∫ c dn_i = ∫ c g_i dμ_i.

2. (Two finite measures.) Put λ₁ := p₁ + n₂ and λ₂ := p₂ + n₁. Both are finite, being sums of finite measures.

3. (Identity (★).) Let c be Borel measurable with |c(x)| ≤ C for all x.
   - c is integrable against each of the finite measures p₁, n₁, p₂, n₂: it is measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, and ‖c(x)‖ ≤ C everywhere (Integrable.of_bound).
   - So the integral is additive in the measure (integral_add_measure):
     ∫ c dλ₁ = ∫ c dp₁ + ∫ c dn₂ and ∫ c dλ₂ = ∫ c dp₂ + ∫ c dn₁.
   - Subtracting and using step 1:
     (★) ∫ c dλ₁ − ∫ c dλ₂ = (∫ c dp₁ − ∫ c dn₁) − (∫ c dp₂ − ∫ c dn₂) = ∫ c g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ c g₂ dμ₂.

4. (λ₁ and λ₂ agree on smooth tests supported in O.) Let ψ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O.
   - ψ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous), hence Borel measurable.
   - Being continuous with compact support, ψ is bounded: there is C with ‖ψ(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
   - By (★) with c = ψ and the hypothesis ∫ ψ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ ψ g₂ dμ₂: ∫ ψ dλ₁ − ∫ ψ dλ₂ = 0, i.e. ∫ ψ dλ₁ = ∫ ψ dλ₂.

5. (Apply the finite-measure uniqueness.) λ₁ and λ₂ are finite measures, O is open, and step 4 holds for every C^∞ ψ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O. Since b vanishes outside O, polyhedral_approx_finite_smooth_ext gives ∫ b dλ₁ = ∫ b dλ₂.

6. (Conclusion.) b is Borel measurable and bounded, so (★) applies with c = b. With step 5:
   ∫ b g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ b g₂ dμ₂ = ∫ b dλ₁ − ∫ b dλ₂ = 0.
   Hence ∫ b g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ b g₂ dμ₂. ∎
proof_key_steps: polyhedral_approx_density_split for (μ₁, g₁) and (μ₂, g₂) gives finite p_i, n_i with ∫ c dp_i − ∫ c dn_i = ∫ c g_i dμ_i for bounded Borel c.
λ₁ := p₁ + n₂ and λ₂ := p₂ + n₁ are finite, and (★) ∫ c dλ₁ − ∫ c dλ₂ = ∫ c g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ c g₂ dμ₂ for bounded Borel c (Integrable.of_bound, integral_add_measure).
(★) and the hypothesis give ∫ ψ dλ₁ = ∫ ψ dλ₂ for C^∞ ψ with compact support in O (smooth ψ is Borel and bounded).
polyhedral_approx_finite_smooth_ext gives ∫ b dλ₁ = ∫ b dλ₂ for b vanishing outside O.
(★) with c = b gives ∫ b g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ b g₂ dμ₂.

audit.reason: The prose and type match all hypotheses and the conclusion. The proof uses precisely the two declared dependencies. Bounded measurability justifies additivity over the finite measures; the resulting difference identity transfers smooth-test agreement and then the conclusion for b. Localization to compact L and b = A.indicator u recovers the selected parent. No circular reliance or deferred proof construction occurs.
